previousBehavior: Each elevated metro car called paintRailVehicleShadow, making three contact ovals on the terrain even though the viaduct supports and deck already cast their own shadows. The existing RISK contract expected both metro and lower train cars to shade the rails, and the changelog described all rail vehicles as shadowed.
intendedBehavior: The elevated electric metro paints all three cars without car shadows in daylight and at night across phone, short-landscape, and tablet geometry. The lower five-car train retains its track-aligned light-responsive footprint; viaduct supports and deck keep their distinct ground shadows. The changelog names this distinction.
replacementTests: RISK landscape vehicles: lower train shadows lie along its rail under changing light
RISK landscape metro: electrified cars have no shadow while viaduct supports keep theirs
preservedCoverage: The shared celestial shadow source still governs grounded visitors, trees, lower train cars, viaduct supports, and deck spans.
Existing lower-train coupler spacing, lower rail contact geometry, day/night palette, narrow and tall viewports, and landscape reduced-motion contracts remain in the suite.
The new metro test counts all rendered cars and their shadow calls at 390x844, 568x320, and 820x1180 in day and night light.

The prior shadow and night-rail contracts explicitly required that extra stripe, so they now distinguish the individual support shadows and visible deck from that continuous shadow.

reason: The user reported a save failure when tapping Undo on iOS in one device. A backup index can fit under the browser's aggregate storage quota while the following restored full-board write cannot. The new tests model the same quota across all localStorage keys and distinguish recyclable automatic history from manual or protected recovery copies.
previousBehavior: Undo could save its optional automatic backup yet fail to write the larger restored board, showing an unsaved-edit warning despite old automatic snapshots occupying storage. Primary saves did not retire backup history on proven quota failure.
intendedBehavior: When Undo's primary write hits aggregate storage quota in one tab, retire the oldest unprotected automatic history and retry the guarded primary write until it succeeds, keeping the newest stable recovery copy. Preserve manual and pinned recovery bytes; if no safe space remains, hold the unsaved edit with an honest warning. The restored title and Start date must survive reload.
replacementTests: RISK LOCAL BACKUPS: single-device Undo frees old automatic history for its primary save
RISK LOCAL BACKUPS: primary quota rotation keeps the newest stable recovery copy
preservedCoverage: Existing cloud adoption and restore backup guards still hold replacement when a safe copy cannot be stored.
Existing concurrent-tab primary and backup-index guards retain newer bytes; this retry only runs after a quota exception while expected primary bytes remain current.
The Undo quota test verifies Start date, title, paired browser keys, reload, protected and manual rows, toast absence after success, and truthful failure when only protected copies remain.
